articleTitle: Advancement in the Mems Gyroscope from a Vibrating Tuning Fork to a Tuned Ring with Comb Electrodes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: Within this paper we report on our development from a MEMS vibrating tuning fork gyroscope to a ring gyroscope with additional comb electrodes for enhanced sensitivity. Since we started from the classical tuning fork gyroscope, we combined elements from this topology with the typical ring structure. We have chosen the ring structure because of the inherent structural equality of the modes and its use for later advanced compensation techniques. This paper presents the design, fabrication and operation of this MEMS ring gyroscope. The results are extracted from measurements with our standard split-mode operation and a fully tuned FM operational mode with independently controlled superposed clockwise and counter clockwise modes.

articleTitle: High Sensitivity Mode-Localized Ring Resonator With Tunable Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a resonator for a mode-localization sensor that offers high and adjustable sensitivity. Two oscillation modes of a fully symmetrical ring resonator are utilized as the dual oscillators for mode-localization sensing. In the proposed resonator, the coupling stiffness, represented as k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>, is determined by both the stiffness mismatch, k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>−k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, and the angle of the principal axis, θ. This stiffness is inversely proportional to the sensitivity. By leveraging electrostatic forces, these parameters can be adjusted, enabling control of the coupling stiffness, which can even approach zero, yielding infinite sensitivity. Experimental results demonstrate that k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> can be adjusted from positive to negative values. The modal shape, represented by the amplitude ratio between the two coordinates, aligns well with mode-localization theory. Furthermore, sensitivity is adjusted using electrostatic tuning. Notably, the sensitivity can be modulated across at least two orders of magnitude.

articleTitle: Robust High-G Microaccelerometers with Mechanical Low-Pass Filters and Electrical ROIC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This paper presents a shock measurement unit (SMU) composed of a cross-symmetric accelerometer core chip, a mechanical low-pass filter, and an electrical read-out integrated circuit (ROIC). The SMU shows a cross-axis sensitivity of less than 1%, a shock endurance as high as 150 kG, and high-frequency shock protection over 100 kHz, demonstrating a high survivability in extreme impact environments.

articleTitle: Characterization of a Passive 3x3 Fiber Optic Gyroscope for Cryogenic Applications at Liquid Nitrogen Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: A fiber optic gyroscope that can operate at room temperature and with its coil submerged in liquid nitrogen was set up and successfully tested. The behavior of long lengths of optical fibers at liquid nitrogen temperatures was investigated. The 3x3 fiber optic gyroscope configuration is discussed and used with modern light sources and analog-digital converters, resulting in the best noise performance of such a device yet.

articleTitle: Symbolic Simulation of Sensor Trimming Algorithms Using Affine Arithmetic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: The quality of trimming and compensation algorithms is key to meet the ever-increasing demands on sensor performance. This work presents an approach to effectively develop and validate trimming algorithms based on symbolic simulation with affine arithmetic (AA). Simulations are performed on intervals to cover a complete parameter space at once. This ensures that the algorithm converges to a correct solution in all cases and not only for a concrete testcase. Moreover, the unique deviation symbols of affine forms allow easy root cause analysis if a trim step has failed. This speeds up the development of new algorithms. However, for classical AA, this is limited to first-order deviation terms. We propose an extension that tracks root causes up to second-order effects, i.e. the combination of two deviation sources. The applicability for industrial cases is shown at the example of a binary search algorithm.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Frequency and Amplitude Stability in A Bulk Acoustic Wave Resonator Based on Amplitude Saturation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: In this paper, the amplitude saturation behavior of a bulk acoustic wave (BAW) resonator operating in the secondary elliptical mode is studied. When the driving force exceeds a specific threshold, the vibration amplitude of the BAW resonator becomes saturated. This nonlinear behavior is controlled by the phase-locked loop (PLL) circuit, and the frequency response curve of the BAW resonator operating in the amplitude saturation state is reconstructed. Furthermore, the frequency instability and amplitude instability of the resonator are compared across various phase. The experimental results indicate that by adjusting the operating point, the frequency instability of 0.14ppb and the amplitude instability of 5.4ppm can be achieved.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Multi-axis Sensitivity and Temperature Compensation for a Physically Tightly-Coupled MEMS IMU Integrating a Mode-Matched Gyroscope and Two Differential Resonant Accelerometers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This paper demonstrates multi-axis sensitivity and temperature compensation for angular velocity, acceleration, and temperature for a mode-matched gyroscope and two differential resonant accelerometers (DRAs) in a single package aimed at realizing a high-precision and compact MEMS inertial measurement unit (IMU). In this evaluation, a mode-matched disk resonator gyroscope (DRG) with Z-axis sensitivity plus a pair of DRAs with X- and Y-axis sensitivity are mounted in a single vacuum-sealed package and evaluated, using analog and digital measurement circuits with three microcontrollers. Multi-axial sensitivity and temperature coefficients were obtained by applying acceleration and angular velocity, and temperature was estimated from the resonance frequency of the devices. Comparing the input/output value errors with and without compensation, it was demonstrated for the first time that multi-axis sensitivity and temperature compensation improved the performance of both the DRG and DRAs. This evaluation result is a major milestone toward the realization of high-precision MEMS IMU.

articleTitle: Technology Platform for High Performance Mems Inertial & Vibration Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: We present a technology platform dedicated to the fabrication of high-performance MEMS accelerometers, gyroscopes, and vibrations sensors for demanding applications. Key features of the platform, called Magelan, are the use of thick single crystalline silicon, a well-controlled Deep Reactive Ion Etching process (DRIE), to minimize frequency mismatch and quadrature, and hermetic wafer level package with the option of high vacuum (<10mTorr) to achieve high Q-factors. It enables the production of innovative designs from single-axis to multi-axis capacitive MEMS inertial and vibration sensor dies with high signal-to-noise ratio. It is one core element of Tronics’ MEMS accelerometers and gyroscopes platform [1], offering outstanding performance for dynamic applications. The Magelan technology is offered to external customers as foundry service with the advantage of fast development cycles and limited technological risks.

articleTitle: Computation of Inertial Signals on Rotational Testbeds
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: Rotational testbeds are ubiquitous in the test and evaluation of inertial sensors and systems. However, the use of rotational testbeds is typically restricted to static states employed over long integration windows to allow for data aggregation. These methods ignore the transitions between states, and data aggregation masks potentially useful signals. In this paper, we discuss the development of modular equations for the description of the inertial inputs to a test sensor using any rotational testbed. Implementing our equations in software, specific force and angular rates can be computed from idealized table motion or measured encoder data. Results are presented using simulated data and measured data. The measured data was acquired using a three axis rate table and a MEMS IMU. The experimental results validate our model equations and demonstrate the benefits of modeling sensor inputs at the sensor rates to compensate for testbed errors.

articleTitle: Nano-g Optical Fiber Accelerometer with Double-Leaf Spring Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: In this paper, a high-resolution optical fiber Fabry -Perot interferometric accelerometer based on a double spring supported spring-mass oscillator for acceleration perception is proposed and demonstrated. Experimental results show that the noise floor is as low as 10 ng/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> at 1 Hz, enabling the two ground pulse peaks to be observed in the noise spectrum. This miniaturized optical fiber accelerometer with high resolution is suitable for low frequency measurements like micro seismic detection and structural health monitoring.

articleTitle: The GYTRIX Quartz Crystal Axisymmetric Mems GYRO: Preliminary measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: On one hand tuning fork type open-loop quartz crystal MEMS gyroscopes achieve tactical - near navigation -grade performances through the excellent temperature and aging stability of quartz resonators, and the linear piezoelectric transduction. On the other hand, recent developments enable silicon based axisymmetric designs to achieve the same thermo-mechanical behavior of the two gyro modes, improving the bias and scale factor stabilities. They also enable matching the two frequencies and then increasing the scale factor in a force rebalance configuration. The axisymmetric quartz crystal MEMS gyro presented here benefits from the advantages of these two kinds of gyro. Its principle of operation as well as a first design and expected performances were reported; the performance objective of this new cell is to achieve a bias repeatability better than 0.1°/h and an ARW < 0.005°/√hr in the closed loop configuration, as well as good immunity to vibrations and thermal variations. The eigen frequency and Q factor variation identity of the two gyro modes are key parameters enabling bias and scale factor stability, this paper reports the experimental validation of the thermomechanical behavior identity between the drive and sense modes of this new axisymmetric quartz crystal gyro. This is the first step towards a high performance quartz crystal closed-loop gyroscope.

articleTitle: North Finding IMU with Electromagnetic MEMS Gyroscope and Mode Reversal Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This paper reports a new north finding inertial unit (NFIMU) with electromagnetic MEMS gyroscope and mode reversal technique. The bias instability is around 0.02deg/h at 5000s averaging time and far below 0.1deg/h even at 40,000s in the Allan Variance measurement. The bias drift over temperature also shows outstanding stability with quintic temperature compensation and it is within +/-0.5deg/h in the temperature range from -15 to 60degC. The azimuth measurement accuracy of this NFIMU successfully achieves the target specification of 1degree(rms).

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of (100) Silicon Ring Gyroscope with Chamfered Rectangle Springs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This paper proposes a theoretical analysis of a MEMS vibratory ring gyroscope (gyro) with chamfered rectangle supporting springs. We developed a MEMS vibratory ring gyro to improve its performance IoT society demands. Its dimensions were optimized by numerical simulation using the finite element method (FEM), which requires computational cost and time. In this study, we have proposed a theoretical analysis method using Castigliano’s method to reduce the calculation cost and time for design optimization. This model includes chamfered rectangle springs which compensate the elastic anisotropy of single crystal silicon. As a result, the proposed theoretical analysis model describes well the relationship between the resonant frequency of each mode and the chamfered part ratio, which agrees well with the FEM simulation. The method has been revealed that it may be useful for design optimization of various ring resonators made of single crystal materials.

articleTitle: Improvements to Calibration Modeling of a Tri-Axial Accelerometer Using Response Surface Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: Aerodynamic ground test facilities require precision attitude measurements to support fundamental research and aerodynamic vehicle characterization. Accelerometers are used as one solution for measuring test article attitude. Several wind-tunnel facilities experience elevated temperatures during sustained testing of approximately 38°C (100°F) and extremes up to 149°C (300°F). Accelerometer thermal corrections are required to maintain attitude measurement accuracy during elevated temperature tunnel conditions. This manuscript details characterization of non-linear and thermal effects of the Mini/MEMs Tri-Axis Sensor System (MTASS) developed at NASA. Non-linear effects are characterized using a two-axis index head, and temperature effects are characterized using a metallic cube in a thermal chamber. The results show a significant decrease in back-computed residuals for room temperature and elevated temperatures experiments.

articleTitle: A Quantum Matterwave Vortex Gyroscope
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: The Vortex Matterwave Gyroscope (VMG) is a new type of quantum rotation sensor based on atom interferometry. The device uses the quantised orbital angular momentum (OAM) of a torus-shaped cold atom cloud to measure rotation angle, giving the device scale factor stability, a robustness to long-term drift, and an advantage over current optical and mat- terwave gyroscope designs due to its primary sensor capabilities and potential atom chip-scale size. In addition, the VMG has a single-shot sensitivity ΔΩ that scales with the OAM imparted to the atom cloud l , the atom cloud population N , and interferometer time T , such that \begin{equation*}\Delta \Omega = \frac{1}{{2lT\sqrt N }}\end{equation*}

articleTitle: Angle White Noise in Vibratory Rate Gyroscopes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This paper presents an in-depth analysis of the origin of angle white noise (AWN) in closed-loop vibratory rotation-rate gyroscopes, and explains the challenges of using the standard Allan deviation (ADEV) method to report AWN results. The modified Allan deviation (MDEV) is then proposed as an alternative for the characterization of devices where AWN is a major noise contributor. Validation of the presented work is performed using measured data from a high-performance BulkAcoustic Wave (BAW) gyroscope, demonstrating how the AWN coefficient can be extracted from the asymptotic response in both ADEV and MDEV plots.

articleTitle: Single Crystal Lithium Niobate Cylindrical Resonator for High-Performance Miniature Piezoelectric Gyroscope
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: In this report, we developed a single crystal lithium niobate cylindrical resonator for piezoelectric vibrating gyroscope of small size and low operating frequency. The cylindrical resonator was fabricated by grinding a 3-mm-thick 155° Y-cut LN wafer. The gold electrodes were patterned using oblique lithography. An electrode on each side of the bottom plate and eight electrodes inside of the cylinder sidewall were designed for 0° and 45° modes, respectively. The impedance spectrum of the fabricated cylindrical resonator observed two wineglass modes around 35 kHz. Operation as a gyroscope was successfully conducted using a digital lock-in amplifier (LIA). The measured bias instability ranged from 133 deg/h to 418 deg/h showing dependence on mode mismatch.

articleTitle: A Dual Atomic Interferometric Inertial Sensor Utilizing Transversely Cooled Atomic Beams
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: Light-pulsed atomic interferometers provide a promising quantum-based solution for inertial navigation applications. In this paper, we present an atomic interferometric inertial sensor designed to simultaneously measure rotation rate and acceleration, through continuous sampling using dual <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">87</sup>Rb atomic beams as matter-wave sources. We observe Raman-Ramsey and Raman-Mach-Zehnder interferences and validate the inertial sensing capability by comparing the results with a classical quartz accelerometer and an optical-fiber gyroscope. Our work can serve as a foundational element for the development of a fully quantum inertial measurement unit characterized with a high data rate and large bandwidth.

articleTitle: GNSS-Denied Pedestrian Navigation Using Machine Learning Aided Gait Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This paper provides experimental results of a GNSS-denied pedestrian navigation system called the Machine Learning Aided Gait Recognition for Inertial Navigation and Orientation (MARIO) system. The MARIO system has a convolutional neural network (CNN) that can estimate a user's velocity data from body-mounted IMUs. An Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) uses the estimated velocity with the IMU data from a back-mounted IMU to estimate position. The MARIO system produced a navigation solution with under 1% error over distance traveled.

articleTitle: Bridging Piezoelectric And Electrostatic Effects:A Novel Pitch/Roll Gyroscope
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel aluminum nitride on silicon (AlN-on-Si) pitch/roll gyroscope with piezoelectric driving/sensing and electrostatic mode-match operation. A 5000 μm annulus resonator gyroscopic with n=2 in-plane (IP) mode and n=3 out-of-plane (OOP) mode. The piezoelectric electrodes are designed based on the operation modes stress to achieve high electromechanical coupling coefficient. Lumped masses and electrostatic electrodes are used to achieve mechanical and electrical mode-match, respectively. After applying a tuning voltage of 66 V, the initial mode split of 170 Hz is almost eliminated, and a scale factor of 64 pA/°/s is obtained, which is 95.3x times higher than that without mode-match operation, demonstrating the feasibility and effectiveness of the design.

articleTitle: Molded Foaming 3D MEMS Vapor Cell for Weak Magnetic Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: A novel MEMS long optical path vapor cell for weak magnetic detection is proposed for the first time. By introducing a simple mold shaping during the thermoforming process, vapor cell with enhanced optical path length, buffer volume and optical transmittance is realized. The molded foaming method is estimated by finite element simulation before fabrication, and a single-beam atomic magnetometer prototype based on the fabricated vapor cell is developed to characterizing the cell performance. Experimental results show that the transmittance of the proposed vapor cell has a 15% improvement, and the magnetic noise floor of the MZ magnetometer is 5.4 pT/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> at 1 Hz under 12000 nT.

articleTitle: High-performance navigation grade resonant beam MEMS accelerometers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This paper reports results obtained from two high-performance navigation grade resonant microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) accelerometer: one with a ±25g dynamic range ("RXL25") and the other with a ±100g dynamic range ("RXL100") demonstrating bias errors of 4 μg and 25 μg respectively over an operational temperature range of -40° to 80°C. The total scale factor (SF) residual errors for both accelerometers over temperature are reported to be less than 2 ppm. The bias instability (BI) and velocity random walk (VRW) of RXL25 are measured to be 0.086 μg and 0.40 $\mu {\text{g}}/\sqrt {{\text{Hz}}} $ respectively. The RXL100 accelerometer yields a BI and VRW of 0.34 μg and 0.91 $\mu {\text{g}}/\sqrt {{\text{Hz}}} $ respectively. The vibration rectification coefficient (VRC) for RXL25 is reported to be less than 10 μg/g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Low Noise Full Digital Phase-Locked Loop with feedthrough Suppression Technology for Resonant Accelerometer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This study presents an integrated digital measurement and control system (DMCS) for the accelerometer, which combines resonator feedthrough prediction and elimination techniques. The bias instability in frequency measurement reaches 170ppt. This system makes the phase change of the accelerometer monotonous, enhancing the stability of the accelerometer.

articleTitle: High Q-Factor and Mode-Matching Disk Ring Gyroscope Using (100) Single Crystal Silicon
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: In this paper, a novel disk ring gyroscope (DRG) was proposed to compensate the anisoelasticity of (100) single crystal silicon (SCS), which can achieve the mode-matching and high Q-factor simultaneously. The proposed DRG consists of two substructure with 4 connection spokes (4-spokes DRG) and an inner nested 8-spokes substructure (8-spokes DRG). After parameter optimization, a frequency split as small as 18 ppm is achieved by the finite element analysis (FEA). The Q-factor of DRG related to thermoelastic damping (Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TED</inf>) reaches 1.36 million. The experimental result showed the frequency split was reduced from over 30,000 ppm to 2015 ppm, which shows a promising DRG design for high performance gyroscope.

articleTitle: Strength Differences of Lateral, Top and Bottom Surface in Monocrystalline Silicon Micromachining
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: The research presents two structures designed to compare the strength of lateral sidewalls against the strength of top and bottom surfaces in a monocrystalline silicon process for MEMS inertial sensors. The first task is achieved through an in-plane driver, with actuation and position-sensing combs, which, through a lever, stresses the vertical surface of a notched specimen. The novel, second task is much harder to accomplish, as vertical gaps and pull-in limit the maximum travel range and achievable stress on horizontal surfaces: it is nevertheless possible to identify a range of strengths between pull-in and the following contact to stoppers in torsional structures with a central notch. Results show a remarkable difference: about 10 GPa strength for lateral surfaces but a noticeably lower value, in the range of 3 GPa to 6 GPa for top and bottom surfaces.

articleTitle: Optical Fiber Displacement Sensor Array with Reduced Sampling Rate for Gravitational Reference Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: In this paper, an optical fiber interferometric displacement sensor array based on time division multiplexing (TDM) is proposed for translation and tilt metrology of gravitational reference sensor (GRS). To effectively reduce the sampling rate, a carrier signal extraction method based on non-uniform sampling is proposed and demonstrated. Experimental result reveals that the sampling rate of 65 MS/s is enough to demodulate the heterodyne carrier signal from a pulse with width of 10 ns, which is 15 times lower than the traditional sampling method.

articleTitle: Active Probe Card for Multi-Parameter Fast Characterization of Mems Gyroscope at Wafer-Level
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This paper proposes a versatile and efficient tool for MEMS gyros offering multi-parameter concerned by both manufacturer and customer at the wafer-level. Two active probe cards (APCs) measure the gyros' static (capacitance and resistance) and dynamic parameters (frequencies, Q-factors, etc) as well as predicted system-level performance (zero-rateoutput (ZRO), zero-quadrature-output (ZQO), etc). The process monitoring parameters and customer-concerned device operating parameters and behaviors under diverse applications with specific Af are automatically extracted from two sequential tests with different voltage loads within 10s per die. System-level characteristic parameters are revalidated, and the gyro's bias-instability (BIS) is also tested after dicing and packaging. The experimental results suggest the proposed APCs could facilitate the best working die selection and system-level performance pre-validation for different application scenarios (e.g., northfinding), at the wafer level.

articleTitle: Map-Based Inertial Navigation for GNSS-Free and Safe Train Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: The paper proposes to exploit the benefits of Inertial Navigation Systems (INS) and details a map-based railway inertial navigation. The method relies on an accurate heading measurement and allows location of the train hybridizing an INS with a digital map without any other sensor such as GNSS or wheel sensor. The map consists of a set of Virtual Georeferenced Heading Beacons (VGHB). Position information is provided to the INS when the measured heading crosses the heading of a VGHB among a selection of eligible VGHB. The position measurement accuracy depends on the VGHB position accuracy and on the precision of the VGHB heading detection which relies on both INS heading accuracy and train mechanical heading repeatability over the tracks. The accuracy and the integrity of the solution is studied on a set of hundreds of hours of GNSS-denied urban data. In 99% of cases the map-based GNSS-free inertial navigation gets less than 1.4 m across errors and less than 3.4 m along errors. It outperforms the solution using the GNSS without the digital map which gets less than 3.2 m across errors and less than 3.6 m along errors.

articleTitle: Nonlinearity Identification of an Integrated Packaged Micro Gyro Operated in a Closed Loop Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: We report on a new approach allowing parameters identification of a closed loop controlled microelectromechanical Coriolis Vibratory Gyroscopes (CVG) driven in a nonlinear regime. Since the drive mode amplitude and phase of the gyro module are both controlled, common nonlinearity identification techniques cannot be directly implemented. The model of an equivalent Duffing oscillator was used for the experimental data fit, for the closed loop control design, and then for the response prediction of devices driven at high amplitudes.

articleTitle: A Mode-localized Resonant Accelerometer Based on A Novel Micro-lever Coupler Resistant to Manufacture Process Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: The mode-localized resonant accelerometer (ML-RXL) described in this study is developed with a unique micro-level mechanical coupling mechanism that protects it from manufacturing process defects and ensures that the coupling stiffness of fabrication is the same as desired value.

articleTitle: A high sensitivity MEMS gravimeter with electrically tunable stiffness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This paper reports on a high sensitivity capacitive micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS) gravimeter. The high sensitivity is achieved by the low resonant frequency structure and large sensing capacitance. An electrical tuning method was employed to reduce the stiffness. The resulting resonance frequency was as small as 1Hz. To attain the large capacitance, a through-silicon Deep-RIE method was applied to a 525μm thick silicon layer. A cascaded demodulation method is adopted in the readout circuit. This capacitive gravimeter demonstrated a sensitivity of 293 pF/g. The voltage sensitivity is 0.96 V⁄Gal. The gravimeter has a noise floor of 0.8$\mu Gal/\sqrt {Hz} $.

articleTitle: Real-Time Scale-factor Calibration for Cold-Atom Gyroscope based on Point-Source Interferometry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: Point-source interferometry (PSI) is a promising technique that enables the realization of compact and multi-axis cold-atom inertial sensors. However, scale-factor errors in the rotational signal, due to the shape and size of the initial atomic distribution, constitute a major drawback. In this paper, we present a method for calibrating the rotational scale-factor. This method relies on the application of a known bias rotation and a compensation scheme that decouples the PSI sensor from the vehicle’s rotational dynamics. We employ a Kalman filter protocol to track the scale-factor error, paving the way for real-time implementation of the calibration method. Through simulations, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the method and the stabilization of the PSI sensor scale-factor.

articleTitle: Passive Quadrature Reduction In Vibratory MEMS BAW Gyroscopes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the design and characterization of a passive quadrature reduction method applied to electrostatic MEMS (Micro-Electro-Mechanical System) BAW (Bulk-Acoustic Wave) gyroscopes. The investigation primarily addresses the challenge of mode-to-mode coupling in axis-symmetric gyroscopes arising from fabrication imperfections. We demonstrate that, when quadrature is caused by a known and reproducible imperfection pattern, introducing a physical bias to the devices across a wafer counteracts the quadrature errors. The core concept involves adding or removing masses, referred to as notches, from the outer periphery of the gyro disk where the displacements from both modes are equal. Our study establishes that this targeted manipulation exclusively affects the stiffness coupling between the two modes. Utilizing measured data, we quantify the impact in terms of stiffness coupling, and by subsequently employing finite element analysis (FEA), we establish the correlation between coupling and the required notch size. By judiciously selecting and implementing the appropriate notches across a wafer, we successfully achieve more than 40% reduction in the standard deviation of quadrature nulling tuning voltage, all while preserving the performance parameters of the gyroscope.

articleTitle: Improving the Temperature Stability of MEMS Gyroscope Bias with on-chip Stress Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: Temperature calibration is commonly used to suppress the bias drift of MEMS inertial sensors. Temperature compensation reduces the bias drift but cannot eliminate it. We report a compensation technique for temperature-induced drifts by incorporating temperature and on-chip stress, for the first time. Adding on-chip stress to the temperature captures the offset behavior with hysteresis more accurately. Our open and closed-loop sense mode temperature sweep results demonstrate almost three-fold offset stability improvement over only temperature calibration for a wide (65°C) temperature range. Temperature and stress sensors provide data about thermal stress and stress mismatches in the sensor stack, respectively. We validate the calibration concept with a MEMS ring gyroscope integrated with eight capacitive stress sensors. We perform the temperature tests with an on-PCB heater that only heats the MEMS die and front-end amplifiers.

articleTitle: Mode-Matched Disk Resonator Gyroscope in (100) Single Crystal Silicon with Shock Resistance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel disk resonator gyroscope (DRG) fabricated in the (100) single crystal silicon (SCS) wafer. The structure consists of an outer anchor, concentric rings, connecting spokes and inner electrodes. It operates in the N=2 wineglass mode, and the translation mode (N=1) has a higher resonant frequency, which reduces the effects of harsh shock environments and maximizes sensitivity. Mode order is achieved by adjusting the inner ring radius and the initial frequency split of the N=2 wineglass mode is reduced by adjusting the spoke angle. The prototype device was fabricated based on Silicon on Insulator (SOI) process. The experimental results of the prototype device validate the proposed novel DRG structure.

articleTitle: On the Optimal Measurement Time in North-Finding Procedures using Maytagging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This article deals with gyro-based North-Finding by using the Maytagging approach. One proposes an analysis of the Maytagging effect on the variance of the estimated azimuth, in function of the gyro disturbances (bias and noise). It is shown that it is preferable to impose a reduced time duration of the Maytagging sequences, and to multiply the number of these sequences.

articleTitle: Simulation-based approach in design of low stress Bowl-shaped Micro Hemispherical Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This paper proposed a numerical simulation framework for the precision molding process to design low-stress Bowl-shaped Micro Hemispherical Resonators(BSRs). The impact of structural designs and process parameters on the internal stress of BSRs was investigates. During the heating stage, a two-dimensional axisymmetric model was established to understand how different structural parameters and bonding pressures affect internal stress. Subsequently, a generalized Newtonian isothermal flow model was established to anticipate the 3D geometries formed during the reflow molding process. Finally, model of cooling stage confirmed that the internal stress in the final formed shell remained within acceptable limits. After optimizing several parameters, the stress within the BSR was reduced to approximately 22 MPa. The simulation-based approach in this study can be used for the optimization of the BSRs’ geometry, achieving increased sphericity while minimizing stress.

articleTitle: Frequency-Comb-like Behavior in a Resonant MEMS Accelerometer Subject to Blue Sideband Excitation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This work reports an intriguing phenomenon discovered when subjecting a differential resonant MEMS accelerometer to blue sideband excitation (BSE). The exhibited behavior is similar to that of phononic frequency combs (PFCs). The experimental data presents a PFC-like spectrum response, with a collection of equidistant fingers when employing BSE. The spacing of the fingers in the induced frequency comb are unaffected by variations in the BSE parameters (i.e., BSE frequency and BSE amplitude), as well as the equivalent input acceleration. On the other hand, the amplitudes of the frequency comb spectral lines are dependent on the BSE signal parameters, and the equivalent acceleration perturbation. This points to a potential sensing scheme which exploits the amplitude changes of the induced frequency combs - which differs from conventional frequency combs that utilize changes in frequency spacing. The underlying mechanism that governs this phenomenon is the subject of ongoing research. This distinctive behavior, which is induced by employing a relatively unexplored operating scheme, is expected to compete with classical amplitude-modulation-based (AM) resonant sensors.

articleTitle: MEMS Underwater Acoustic Vector Sensor Operating in Near Neutral Buoyancy Configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This paper reports on the functionality of an acoustic vector sensor (AVS) for underwater use. The AVS is comprised of two micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS) acoustic directional sensors coupled with an omnidirectional hydrophone and can determine direction of arrival (DOA) of acoustic waves in water. The MEMS sensors are contained in air-filled, water-tight housings and are operated in a nearly neutrally buoyant configuration. In this configuration, the acoustic sensors act as inertial sensors, detecting the vibration of the housing rather than the pressure wave directly. This paper discusses the design of the AVS as well as its DOA accuracy. The AVS demonstrated an average DOA error, over a full 360-degree azimuth, as low as 7.8 degrees.

articleTitle: On Temperature Effects in a MEMS Ring Gyroscope
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: We report on experimental and analytical investigation of temperature effects in a 3.2mm-diameter, 57kHz ring gyroscope equipped with 16 capacitive stress sensors. According to the well-known ~-60ppm/°C temperature dependency of Young’s modulus of silicon, the temperature coefficient of frequency (TCF) is expected to be ~-30ppm/°C. Our experimentally observed TCFs, however, tend to be ~-14ppm/°C, pointing to thermal stresses as the countering factor. To find the root cause of the measured TCFs, we develop an analytical framework that enables us to calculate the temperature-induced stiffness variations, considering both thermal and mechanical strains. The model successfully predicts changes and hysteretic behavior of frequency over temperature using the measured stress and temperature data.

articleTitle: Upgrading a gyroscope from a lab-based setup into a pre-industrial demo: challenges and lessons learned
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This work reports advancements in MEMS gyroscopes based on NEMS resistive detection, towards a prototype demonstration in operational environment. The developed system relies on two chips (the microelectromechanical system itself and a low-noise front-end integrated circuit), off-the-shelf analog to digital (A/D) and digital to analog (D/A) converters, and, for the first time on such gyroscopes, on-board demodulation, and signal processing with no need for external instrumentation. These tasks are performed with a field-programmable gate array (FPGA), also implementing tracking of the drive frequency as an estimate of temperature. At 5-V supply, the system communicates to PC via USB or RS422 and yields 0.006 °/√hr angle random walk and sub-0.02 °/hr stability.

articleTitle: Vibration Rectification Error Reduction in Mems Vibrating Beam Accelerometers by Using the F-Squared Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: We present on the results of vibration rectification measurements for low-noise MEMS vibrating beam accelerometers (VBAs) [1] with a dynamic range of ± 25g. We introduce an experimental setup designed for precise and repeatable measurement of VRE using random vibration tests. These tests demonstrate scale factor non-linearity (SFNL) to be dominant contribution to vibration rectification error (VRE). In this paper, we demonstrate a significant reduction in SFNL and consequently the VRE coefficient by employing the f-squared method. This results in the demonstration of accelerometers with both high and low bias demonstrating a low measured VRE < 10 µg/g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Stress Reduction by Indirect Bonding Configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative indirect bonding anchor structure designed to enhance the final test trimming accuracy of capacitive MEMS accelerometers. In a comprehensive study involving 768 teeter-totter accelerometers, the proposed anchor configuration successfully reduces the offset from an initial -158.1mG to a significantly improved -4.5mG.

articleTitle: Auxiliary Gyroscope Approach for Balanced Performance via Gyro Self-Calibration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: Gyro noise and bias are often performance limiting factors in space and terrestrial navigation systems, especially in cases where no aiding sensors are available. A gyro unit with good performance in both noise and bias may be very expensive and with undesirable SWaP. In this paper, we propose to make use of the self-calibrating capabilities of an inexpensive MEMS Coriolis Vibratory Gyros (CVG) gyro as an auxiliary sensor for a set of primary gyros of any type, including those not capable of self-calibrating, to greatly reduce the biases of the primary and auxiliary gyros, as the primary gyros' biases can all be made observable and calibratable using the auxiliary CVG's self-calibration capability in real-time without impacting the normal use of the primary gyros. The combined gyro system can therefore retain the good noise performance of the primary gyros while greatly improving on its bias stability performance.

articleTitle: A CNN-LSTM Model for IMU-based Energy Expenditure Estimation under Various Walking Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: Energy expenditure (EE) is important quantities in evaluating the intensity of physical activity and health status. EE can be estimated based on signals from wearable sensors such as inertial measurement unit (IMU) and electromyography (EMG) sensor. Although many algorithms have been developed to estimate EE during daily life [1] – [4] , only a few algorithms have evaluated the performance of EE according to walking conditions (speed and incline) [2] – [4] . This paper presents a combined model of convolutional neural network (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) for an IMU-based EE estimation under various walking conditions. The results of this study suggest the optimal IMU location for estimating EE during level walkings/runnings and inclined walkings.

articleTitle: Precision Mode-Matching Gyroscope using In-Run Adjustment of Spring Azimuth
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: This paper presents a novel precision mode-matching method for Coriolis vibratory gyroscopes with high-Q resonator by adjusting the angle of spring azimuth (θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ω</inf>) using quad demodulation with dual PLL. The proposed method can control the frequency difference (Δf) between the drive and sense resonant frequencies more precisely compared with conventional modematching methods because Δf can be directly measured and θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ω</inf> can be independently measured and adjusted during the gyroscopic operation. By applying this method to shell-type resonators having a Q-factor of 230,000 with an initial θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ω</inf> of 23 degrees and Δf of 1.6 Hz, θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ω</inf> can be controlled within 0.013 degrees, thus Δf of 2.02 mHz at 1σ was achieved. This result shows an improvement in accuracy of about 5 times over the conventional mode-matching accuracy of 10mHz [1].

articleTitle: Real Time Mismatch Monitoring Using Software Defined Frequency Modulation and Rate Integrating Gyroscope
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Inertial Sensors and Systems (INERTIAL)
abstract: In this paper, we present a software-defined frequency modulation and rate integrating gyroscope (SD-FM/RIG) using a doughnut mass resonator (DMG). A control system including CW/CCW demodulators, numerically controlled oscillators, and feedback controllers was implemented as the software in a micro processing unit (MPU). We demonstrated the independent control of two degenerated eigenmodes. Furthermore, we implemented a method to detect mismatches in the resonator based on amplitude modulation and demodulation techniques. The mismatches were successfully detected, continuously recorded for over 1 hour, and observed to shift in value.
